summary: Qualification passed every deterministic and semantic case.

requirementAssessments.evidence: In src/instructions.ts, loadSupportInstruction and loadSummaryInstruction read the corresponding canonical support and summary instruction.md files. In src/agents.ts, those loaders are bound directly to supportAgent and summaryAgent respectively. The actor accurately reports these relationships, and deterministic inspection reports status valid.

moldea/moldea.yaml binds supportAgent to SupportOutputSchema and find-order to findOrderTool, findOrder, FindOrderInputSchema, and FindOrderOutputSchema. src/agents.ts binds SupportOutputSchema, registers findOrderTool, and declares handoffs as both summaryAgent and configuredSummaryHandoff; src/tools.ts closes the registration-to-implementation and schema chain. The actor reports all these relationships consistently.

Workspace assertions show identical before/after hashes and no changed paths, preserving src/implementations.ts. The actor explicitly states that no agent or provider was invoked and that runtime execution, schema enforcement, routing or handoff execution, subagent behavior, and agent input schemas remain unproven; adapter evidence is characterized as detection only. Deterministic evidence also reports repositoryUnchanged true and a passing typecheck.
Runner checks passed: deterministic-after, workspace-assertions.

requirementAssessments.evidence: The actor report identifies the prior canonical `find_order` versus source-established `lookup_order` mismatch. Current `src/tools.ts` declares `name: 'lookup_order'`, and the runner-owned workspace assertions confirm only `moldea/moldea.yaml` changed.

`moldea/moldea.yaml` now declares `name: lookup_order`, exactly matching `src/tools.ts`. Workspace assertions show `moldea/moldea.yaml` as the sole changed path while `src/agent.ts`, `src/tools.ts`, `src/implementations.ts`, and `src/contracts.ts` retain identical before/after hashes. Deterministic inspect and validate statuses are both `valid`, with no failures.

The manifest binds runtime agent `supportAgent` and instruction loader `loadSupportInstruction` in `/src/agent.ts`, registration `lookupOrderTool` in `/src/tools.ts`, implementation `lookupOrder` in `/src/implementations.ts`, and both `LookupOrderInputSchema` and `LookupOrderOutputSchema` in `/src/contracts.ts`. Repository source confirms the direct `Agent`, closed `[lookupOrderTool]` array, function-tool registration, implementation, and schemas. Runner assertions prove all these files are unchanged; deterministic inspection is valid and typechecking passed. The actor explicitly limits adapter evidence to static wiring and leaves runtime execution unproven.
Runner checks passed: deterministic-after.

The actor report explicitly treats those adapter-unsupported relationships as absent, consistent with the current workspace and valid deterministic result.

src/agents.ts constructs dynamic-support from the indirect `dynamicSupportConfiguration`, builds transformed handoff text with `.join`, and separately constructs a `RealtimeAgent`. The manifest does not record definition-derived routing, handoff, schema, or RealtimeAgent relationships. It retains `indirect-agent-configuration` as a warning stating that an Agent definition and its relationships cannot be proven, with resolution through a closed inline configuration or supported adapter pattern. The actor report explains the same limitation. Before/after hashes are identical and changedPaths is empty.
